newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Konka sees slightly higher net for '96.
newsitem.headline: Konka sees slightly higher net for '96.

text.p: Chinese television maker Shenzhen Konka Electronic Group Co Ltd is likely to report a marginal rise in its 1996 net profits due to stronger sales, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

"Konka saw stronger operations in the second half of 1996 as sales picked up as a result of lower prices for its televisions," the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin. He declined to give figures.
Konka reported after-tax profits of 265.06 million yuan for 1995, up 17 percent from 226.71 million yuan the previous year, under Chinese accounting standards.
In early June 1996, Konka reduced its prices by an average 10 percent to match price cuts in March by its main competitor, Sichuan Changhong Electric Appliance Co Ltd.

Konka's unaudited interim net for 1996 edged up 1.7 percent year-on-year to 142.67 million yuan, with sales jumping 21 percent to 2.03 billion yuan. Konka said its moves to expand market share by lowering the price of most television models had boosted sales but squeezed profit margins.
In its interim report, Konka said it had 11.8 percent of the mainland China market, up from nine percent last year.
